messages.subject: base href, relative URLs
parts:
I have an app with two Rmd files run by shiny that I'd like people to be able to click between. Call them a.Rmd and b.Rmd.

When I have a (relative) link to b.Rmd from a.Rmd, the base href is added on and it becomes something like:

https://blah.shinyapps.io/app/_w_f974a5b7/b.Rmd.

This works fine, until I try to click back to a.Rmd from b.Rmd. Then, the URL becomes

https://blah.shinyapps.io/app/_w_f974a5b7/_w_f974a5b7/a.Rmd.

because the base href is added on a second time. This link fails with an internal server error.

Of course, this is easy to get around by constructing absolute URLs, but I was wondering what the purpose of the base href is in this case? Does it keep the server from starting new instances? Does it keep track of users?

Is there any way to work around this with relative URLs?

Is there any drawback to working around this with absolute URLs? (e.g., more simultaneous sessions are created)

Thanks,
Richard

messages.author: e84e7628b5f8a3e1
messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Re: base href, relative URLs
parts:
FYI, The purpose of the base-ref is identify the session (requests will be routed to the same shiny session by the worker).

As for how to deal with your links, you might try posting this question to shiny-discuss user group.

-Andy
